sentences.text:
It has been alleged that the petitioner No. 2 is aggrieved of FIR No. 0017/2024 dated 23.12.2024,
under Sections 85, 115(2), and 3(5) of the BNS 2023 registered by respondent No. 2-Station House Officer, Police Station, Women Cell, Kathua at the instance of petitioner No. 1, and the same is based on vague and baseless allegations without any reasonable grounds to establish an offence against petitioner No. 2 and his family.
3. It has been further asserted in the petition that the marriage between the petitioners was solemnized in the year 2020 as per Muslim rites and customs and they were living peacefully and one male child was born out of their wedlock; that the petitioner No. 2 is serving in the Indian Army and has constructed a separate house in his native village, Sumbli Kahara Bari Barhamna, Samba,
where petitioner No.1 is living separately from her in-laws; that on 20.12.2024 a minor domestic dispute arose between the petitioners, as a result of which, the petitioner No. 1 left her matrimonial home and went to Kathua where she moved an application against petitioner No. 2 and his family members for registration of an FIR and the respondent No. 2 without adopting due course of law and conducting any preliminary enquiry as mandated by the Hon'ble Apex Court, registered the impugned FIR, as mentioned supra; that the petitioner No. 2 is an army personnel and the co-accused are his old aged parents and younger brother, who is a student.

It is submitted in the petition that after consultations with respectable persons of family and local individuals, the petitioners now have decided to settle the dispute amicably and on 29.03.2025 the petitioners entered into a compromise agreement and filed this petition before this Court for quashing the impugned FIR (supra).
4.

Lastly, the petitioners have prayed before this Court to allow this petition by issuing appropriate order for quashing of FIR No. 0017/2024 dated 23.12.2024, under Sections 85, 115(2) and 3(5) of BNS 2023 registered by respondent No. 2-Station House Officer, Police Station, Women Cell,
Kathua, on the instance of petitioner No. 1 for disposal under law and all consequential proceedings on the basis of compromise agreement dated 29.03.2025.
5. This Court, vide order dated 04.04.2025, directed examination of the parties in support of the compromise placed on record.
The statements of the parties have been recorded, who have supported the contentions made in the compromise.
6. It is stated by learned counsel for the petitioners that the parties have entered into a compromised and prayed that the petition be allowed.
His statement is taken on record.

7. Since the petitioner No.2 who is accused in an FIR registered at the instance of petitioner No.
1-who is the wife of petitioner No. 2, have resolved their dispute by entering into a compromise, no purpose shall be served in case the FIR in question is not quashed by this Court and the parties are made to run through the mill of trial before a court which shall be almost a mock trial resulting into acquittal wasting the time of the parties and serving no cause of justice.

sentences.text: The scope of powers exercisable by the High Court in its inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is no longer res integra.

The Apex Court in the case reported as B.S. Joshi & Ors v. State of Haryana & Anr, (2003 Cri.L.J. 2028) held as under:-
"14.There

entities.text: B.S. Joshi & Ors v. State of Haryana & Anr, (2003 Cri.L.J. 2028)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: is no doubt that the object of introducing Chapter XX-A containing Section 498A in the Indian Penal Code was to prevent the torture to a woman by her husband or by relatives of her husband.
Section 498A was added with a view to punishing a husband and his relatives who harass or torture the wife to coerce her or her relatives to satisfy unlawful demands of dowry.
The hyper-technical view would be counter productive and would act against interests of women and against the object for which this provision was added.
There is every likelihood that non exercise of inherent power to quash the proceedings to meet the ends of justice would prevent women from settling earlier.
That is not the object of Chapter XXA of Indian Penal Code.

15. In view of the above discussion, we hold that the High Court in exercise of its inherent powers can quash criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint and Section 320 of the Code does not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 of the Code."
The aforesaid view of the Apex Court in the judgment (supra) has subsequently been reiterated in Narinder Singh & Ors vs. State of Punjab & Anr, (2014(6) SCC 466).

entities.text: Narinder Singh & Ors vs. State of Punjab & Anr, (2014(6) SCC 466)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the aforementioned cases and in view of the statements having been made by learned counsel for the petitioners that the parties have entered into a compromise, the investigation in the FIR in question would serve no fruitful purpose.

Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and the impugned FIR No. 0017/2024 dated 23.12.2024 under Sections 85, 115(2) and 3(5) of BNS 2023 registered by respondent No. 2-Station House Officer, Police Station, Women Cell, Kathua, alongwith all consequential proceedings, is quashed.
10. Disposed of, accordingly.
